name: Navratan Korma
equipment: Kadai or heavy pan with lid: the base of the whole dish
Small saucepan for boiling the vegetables
Mixer-grinder or hand blender for the smooth paste
Chopping board and knife, small bowl for soaking, measuring spoons, kitchen scale

steps.title: Soak the cashews
steps.text: Put 15 g cashews in a small bowl with 50 ml hot water.
steps.visualCue: Cashews look plump and slightly soft
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of cashews in water

steps.title: Dice the hard vegetables
steps.text: Cut 30 g carrot and 30 g potato into 1 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Even cubes, so they cook at the same speed
steps.cameraCheck: The cubes on the board next to a ruler or coin

steps.title: Cut the beans and cauliflower
steps.text: Cut 25 g beans into 1 cm pieces and 30 g cauliflower into small florets.
steps.visualCue: Pieces roughly the size of the carrot cubes
steps.cameraCheck: All chopped vegetables in one bowl

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics and paneer
steps.text: Chop 3 g ginger, 3 g garlic and ½ green chilli roughly. Cut 30 g paneer into 2 cm cubes and chop 15 g pineapple small.
steps.visualCue: Small bits of ginger and garlic, white paneer cubes
steps.cameraCheck: The paneer cubes and chopped aromatics on the board
steps.videoShot: Paneer cubes sliding off the knife.

steps.title: Boil the vegetables
steps.text: In a saucepan bring 200 ml water with a pinch of salt to a boil. Add carrot, potato, beans and cauliflower and simmer 4 min, then add 20 g peas and simmer 2 min more.
steps.tip: Under-cook slightly; they cook again in the gravy.
steps.visualCue: A knife tip goes in with light resistance; the vegetables keep their colour and shape
steps.cameraCheck: A fork piercing a carrot cube
steps.videoShot: Colourful vegetables bubbling in the pan.

steps.title: Drain the vegetables
steps.text: Drain in a sieve, keeping 4 tbsp (60 ml) of the cooking water.
steps.cameraCheck: The drained vegetables and the saved water

steps.title: Fry the paneer
steps.text: Heat 5 g (1 tsp) oil in the kadai on medium for 1 min. Fry the paneer cubes for 2 min, turning, until lightly golden on two sides. Lift out onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Light golden edges, no dark brown
steps.cameraCheck: The golden paneer on the plate

steps.title: Fry the nuts and raisins
steps.text: Add 5 g (1 tsp) ghee to the same pan on low. Fry 5 g cashews for 30 sec until pale gold, then 5 g raisins for 10 sec until they puff. Lift both out onto the plate.
steps.tip: Cashews burn fast; take them out while still pale.
steps.visualCue: Cashews pale gold, raisins puffed and plump

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: In the fat left in the pan, on low heat, add the bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. Stir for 30 sec.
steps.visualCue: A sweet spice smell, the cloves swell slightly
steps.videoShot: Whole spices sizzling in the fat.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and a pinch of salt. Cook on medium-low for 4–5 min, stirring, until soft and translucent but not brown.
steps.visualCue: Soft, glassy onion with no brown edges (white gravy)

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the chopped ginger, garlic and green chilli and stir for 1 min.
steps.visualCue: A raw smell turns to a warm one

steps.title: Cool and remove the whole spices
steps.text: Add 100 ml water and simmer 3 min. Fish out the bay leaf and cinnamon, switch off the heat and cool 5 min.
steps.tip: Never blend a very hot mixture; steam can push the lid off.
steps.cameraCheck: The bay leaf and cinnamon on a plate
steps.videoShot: Spoon lifting the bay leaf out.

steps.title: Blend the paste
steps.text: Tip the onion mixture and the soaked cashews with their soaking water into a blender. Blend 1–2 min until completely smooth.
steps.visualCue: A pale, silky paste with no grit when rubbed between fingers
steps.cameraCheck: A spoon of paste held up

steps.title: Cook the paste with the powders
steps.text: Pour the paste back into the pan on low heat. Add 0.5 g turmeric, 1 g Kashmiri chilli and 1.5 g coriander powder. Cook 3 min, stirring constantly.
steps.tip: If it splutters or sticks, add 1 tbsp water.
steps.visualCue: The raw smell goes and the paste thickens slightly

steps.title: Add milk and water
steps.text: Pour in 50 ml milk and the saved vegetable water (60 ml). Stir and simmer on low for 3 min.
steps.visualCue: A smooth gravy that coats the back of a spoon

steps.title: Add vegetables and pineapple
steps.text: Add the boiled vegetables, pineapple and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt. Simmer covered on low for 4 min.
steps.visualCue: Gravy bubbling gently around the vegetables

steps.title: Finish with paneer, cream and garam masala
steps.text: Add the fried paneer, 15 g (1 tbsp) cream and 0.5 g garam masala. Stir gently and warm for 1 min. Do not boil hard.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, creamy, pale-ivory gravy; no oil slick, no curdled bits
steps.cameraCheck: The finished curry in the pan

steps.title: Garnish and rest
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Scatter the fried cashews, raisins and 2 g coriander leaves. Rest covered for 2 min.
steps.visualCue: Glossy gravy with golden nuts on top
steps.videoShot: Nuts and raisins dropping on the korma.

reasons: a good variety of vegetables (about 135 g), some protein from paneer and cashew, and no frying of the vegetables. Points off because it is a rich dish: about 31 g fat, with saturated fat about 14 g (ghee, paneer, cream, cashew), plus sweetness from raisins and pineapple and moderate sodium (about 650 mg). Restaurant versions commonly add more cream, butter, khoya and sugar, so 550–700 kcal bowls with 15 g or more saturated fat are common (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published restaurant-menu staple. Veg Recipes of India, Indian Healthy Recipes, Archana's Kitchen, Yummy Tummy, Gulf News, MasterClass and many others publish it, and Wikipedia's korma article lists it as a standard vegetarian korma ("nine gems"). Points off because it is rich and sweet, many reviewers say restaurant versions are heavy, and it is not an everyday home dish. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezing is not recommended: the paneer turns crumbly and the cream gravy can split on thawing. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water or milk, stirring gently, until just steaming; or microwave covered in 1-minute bursts. The gravy thickens overnight, so loosen it.
leftoverRemix: Navratan korma kathi roll. Cook the leftover korma down until it is very thick and dry. Spread green chutney on a warm roti, add the korma, sliced onion and a squeeze of lemon, roll tight and toast on a tawa with ½ tsp oil.
burnOff: about 6.9 km of running (480 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 9.6 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 55 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 660 kcal): about 9.4 km running or 13.2 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: onion, garlic, table salt and garam masala are out under the common rule set; use sendha namak, keep potato, carrot, paneer, nuts, pineapple and raisins, and leave out peas, beans and cauliflower (assumption: the common rule set; families differ).

ekadashi.reason: no grains or pulses in the dish, but peas and beans are legumes and onion and garlic are avoided; cook the Sattvik variant with only potato, carrot and paneer and use sendha namak (common rule set).

jain.reason: the main recipe uses onion, garlic, fresh ginger, potato and carrot; cook the Jain variant.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; it is a rich, filling curry with roti for iftar dinner. Sodium is moderate (about 650 mg) and the dish is heavy, so keep the portion small at sehri.

jain.reason: drop onion, garlic, fresh ginger, potato and carrot; use the Jain variant (cashew-almond base, beans, peas, capsicum and cauliflower, hing for flavour).

vegan.reason: ghee, paneer, milk and cream are dairy; use the Vegan variant (oil, tofu, coconut milk and cashew cream).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: leave out onion, garlic and green chilli paste; use the Sattvik variant (cashew-poppy-ginger-powder base).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida or rava, and the recipe uses no hing; check the garam masala label for added flour. Most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so use gluten-free hing if you add any.

dairyFree.reason: dairy is ghee 5 g, paneer 30 g, milk 50 ml and cream 15 g; use the Dairy-free variant.
